title: Accessibility: keyboard play, screen-reader labels, reduced motion
description: A real accessibility pass: the entire UI is operable by keyboard, every control has a screen-reader label, toasts/prompts are announced, and a reduced-motion mode disables shakes, slow-mo, and particle FX.
acceptanceCriteria: Keyboard-only play: every UI action (claims screen, chart, menus, panels, chat, prompts, weapon select, target lock/release) is reachable and executable with keyboard alone (Tab/Enter/arrows/number keys/E/T/1/2/M/ESC); a keyboard-only e2e run (no mouse events at all) completes: claim → join → open chart → warp → dock → disembark → mine → re-enter → sell (the full loop, scripted keys)

Screen-reader labels: every interactive element has an accessible name (aria-label or visible label); HUD status values (speed, hull, credits, exposure) are exposed via an aria-live='polite' region updated at 1 Hz (not 10 Hz — no announcement spam): 'Speed 120 meters per second. Hull 80 percent.'; prompts are announced ('E to take iron, 3 units')
Toasts and combat events are announced (aria-live): joins/leaves, kills, 'target locked', 'low energy'; announcements are queued (max 1 pending, 2 s min interval) so combat doesn't flood the SR

Reduced motion (a settings toggle, TASK-55, default off): disables camera shake, slow-mo, particle FX (debris/smoke/trails), screen-edge threat ping animation (static icon instead), and the warp streak (a simple fade instead); the toggle takes effect immediately (no restart)

Focus management: the focus trap (TASK-53) works; on menu open, focus moves to the panel's first control; on close, focus returns to the trigger; the game canvas has an aria-label ('3D view: flying in system X') and role='img'
Contrast: all text meets WCAG AA (4.5:1) against its background — a contrast test (computed from the design tokens) asserts every token pair passes

Tests: the keyboard-only e2e (the headline test), aria-label coverage (a test walks the DOM of every screen state and asserts no unlabeled interactive elements), live-region update content (1 Hz assertion), reduced-motion (FX count = 0 when on, verified via the FX registry counter), focus trap + restore; npm run test green

steps.details: tests/e2e/keyboardOnly.spec.ts: the full loop with keyboard events only (the TASK-70 harness); each step asserts the expected UI state change (DOM) — this test is the project's a11y proof.

Audit every component (claims, chart, menus, panels, HUD, prompts): add aria-labels; the LiveRegion component (1 Hz summarizer reading game state); the announcement queue (priority: combat > navigation > chat).

The settings flag (TASK-55's store, defined here as a shared setting key) → an FX gate in the fx registry (TASK-43 fx, TASK-49 explosion, TASK-27 handoff shake): when on, FX are skipped (the registry counter exposes the skip count for the test); the threat ping renders a static icon.
Token-pair contrast test (a small script over the design tokens in src/client/ui/theme.ts); focus trap/restore component test; run full suite + e2e.

technicalNotes: The 1 Hz live region is the key SR decision: announcing at 10 Hz is unusable; a 1 Hz summary is the standard game-a11y pattern.
The keyboard-only e2e is also a regression test for input gating (TASK-53) — keep it fast (< 60 s).
No audio in v1 (PRD scope) — the SR live region is the accessibility channel; audio cues are post-v1.
